note: An experiment (GAME_SPEC §13.7, Stage 85; docs/CURRICULUM.md, experiment 44) on data/benches/ksp.json: calcium hydroxide's solubility product, in water and with a common ion. Ca(OH)2(s) <=> Ca2+ + 2 OH-; Ksp = [Ca2+][OH-]^2; each filtrate's hydroxide titrated with 0.0500 M HCl.
title: Experiment: the solubility product of calcium hydroxide

report.label: [OH-] in water
report.why: [OH-] = c V / 25.00 mL: the acid's 0.0500 M times the burette's difference, over the pipette's 25.00 mL.

report.label: Ksp from water
report.truth: (1000 * filtrate_a.calcium_ion.mol / filtrate_a.condensed_ml) * (1000 * filtrate_a.hydroxide_ion.mol / filtrate_a.condensed_ml) * (1000 * filtrate_a.hydroxide_ion.mol / filtrate_a.condensed_ml)
report.why: In water each Ca2+ came with two OH-: [Ca2+] = [OH-] / 2, so Ksp = [OH-]^3 / 2. A table's Ksp (about 5e-6 at 25 C) is the product of activities; the product of concentrations is several times it, as the ions' atmospheres hold them in the solution.

report.label: [OH-] in 0.100 M calcium chloride
report.why: The same titration of filtrate B.

report.label: the common ion
report.why: Le Chatelier: the calcium already in the solution pushes Ca(OH)2(s) <=> Ca2+ + 2 OH- back toward the solid. Less dissolves, though not as much less as [Ca2+][OH-]^2 held to water's would say: the chloride's ions also lower each ion's activity.

steps.title: Funnel A on its beaker
steps.text: Pick up filter funnel A and click the beaker "filtrate A".
steps.why: Only the clear solution is titrated: a grain of the solid would take acid too and read as dissolved.

steps.title: The solution in water through it
steps.text: Pick up the bottle "calcium hydroxide in water", right-click funnel A, type 60 and click "pour".

checks.text: about 60 mL poured into funnel A

steps.title: Funnel B on its beaker
steps.text: Pick up filter funnel B and click the beaker "filtrate B".

steps.title: The solution in calcium chloride through it
steps.text: Pick up the bottle "calcium hydroxide in 0.100 M calcium chloride", right-click funnel B, type 60 and click "pour". Then click 60x on the clock.

checks.text: about 60 mL poured into funnel B

steps.title: Until both have run through
steps.text: Watch the beakers fill with the clear filtrates.

steps.title: The funnels away
steps.text: Pick up funnel A and click a free square; then funnel B.

steps.title: 25.00 mL of filtrate A
steps.text: Click 1x on the clock. Pick up the pipette and click filtrate A: it draws to its mark. Then click flask A: it stands in the flask and drains.
steps.why: A pipette delivers its 25.00 mL within 0.03 mL: the volume every result is divided by.

steps.title: Until it is empty
steps.text: Watch the pipette drain.

steps.title: 25.00 mL of filtrate B
steps.text: Pick up the pipette, click filtrate B, then click flask B.

steps.title: Until it is empty
steps.text: Watch the pipette drain.

steps.title: The pipette away
steps.text: Pick up the pipette and click a free square.

steps.title: Phenolphthalein in both
steps.text: Pick up the phenolphthalein, right-click flask A, type 0.15 and click "pour". Then the same into flask B.
steps.why: Phenolphthalein is pink above pH 9: the hydroxide holds the flasks pink until the acid has taken it all.

steps.title: Fill the burette
steps.text: Pick up the acid, right-click the burette, type 55 and click "pour". Then right-click the burette and click "+ mL".

steps.title: The burette over flask A
steps.text: Pick up the burette and click flask A.

steps.title: Most of it, fast
steps.text: Right-click the burette and drag its tap to about 30 %.
steps.why: About 20 mL will be needed: the first 15 can run in fast.

steps.title: To 15 mL
steps.text: Watch the burette until it reads 15 mL.

steps.title: Then drop by drop
steps.text: Drag the burette's tap nearly shut, to about 4 %.

steps.title: Until the pink is gone
steps.text: Watch flask A until it turns colourless.

steps.title: Shut it, and read it
steps.text: Drag the tap shut, then right-click the burette and click "+ mL".

steps.title: Fill it again
steps.text: Pick up the burette and click a free square. Pick up the acid, right-click the burette, type 30 and click "pour". Then right-click the burette and click "+ mL".

steps.title: The burette over flask B
steps.text: Pick up the burette and click flask B, then drag its tap to about 30 %.

steps.title: To 10 mL more
steps.text: Watch the burette until it reads 10 mL more than it did.

steps.title: Then drop by drop
steps.text: Drag the burette's tap nearly shut, to about 4 %.

steps.title: Until the pink is gone
steps.text: Watch flask B until it turns colourless.

steps.title: Shut it, and read it
steps.text: Drag the tap shut, then right-click the burette and click "+ mL".
